Objects.name: ULSDVOBJ_EIGC_BLE_Debug_v1
Objects.description: BMD-345 radio state. This is the secondary telemetry channel to the drone, specified to about 1000 m, over which the platform centre position and velocity are broadcast so the drone can close on the platform until the IR landing system acquires it. The telemetry leg is connectionless - the counters below are beacons sent and heard, not a connection - while the service leg is a GATT connection carrying the ULS bus for a PC. See devs-nrf/RADIO.md

variables.name: bleStatus
variables.description: State of the module, of the telemetry broadcast and of the service link

variables.name: linkState
variables.description: State of the telemetry leg. Broadcasting means this unit is transmitting; Tracking means it is also hearing an accepted peer

variables.name: rssi
variables.description: Signal strength of the last accepted peer beacon. The one number that says whether the range budget is holding

variables.name: txPower
variables.description: Transmit power currently in use

variables.name: peerSerial
variables.description: Serial number of the peer being tracked, from its beacon. The ULS serial, not a Bluetooth address - the BLE address is derived from it and is of no interest to an operator

variables.name: peerDistance
variables.description: Distance from the platform centre to the tracked peer, computed from the position in its beacon. Sanity check on whether the link range matches the geometry

variables.name: peersHeard
variables.description: Distinct peers whose beacons were accepted in the last few seconds. In a zone with several platforms and several drones this is the number that says whether the airtime budget is being met - it is not 0 or 1 in normal operation

variables.name: beaconsSent
variables.description: Telemetry beacons transmitted since power on

variables.name: beaconsRx
variables.description: Beacons received and accepted since power on

variables.name: beaconsRejectedFleet
variables.description: Beacons dropped for a foreign fleetId. Expected to be non-zero wherever another operator shares the zone; a large number is information, not a fault

variables.name: beaconsRejectedAuth
variables.description: Beacons of this fleet whose signature failed. Any non-zero value here means either a mis-provisioned unit or someone transmitting who should not be - the two are told apart by beaconsRejectedEpoch

variables.name: beaconsRejectedEpoch
variables.description: Beacons rejected because the sender's keyEpoch differs from this unit's. This is what a half-finished rekey looks like

variables.name: beaconsRejectedReplay
variables.description: Beacons whose signature verified but which were stale or out of sequence - a replay, or a peer whose GNSS time is wrong

variables.name: lastBeaconAge
variables.description: Time since the last accepted peer beacon. Compare against beaconMaxAge in the config object

variables.name: lastTelemetryAge
variables.description: Time since the STM32 last supplied a platform position for this unit to broadcast. A stale value here means the fault is on the wire, not in the air

variables.name: serviceConnectCount
variables.description: Service connections established since power on

variables.name: serviceRejectCount
variables.description: Service connections dropped for failing to authenticate, and privileged ULS bus commands refused on an unauthenticated link

variables.name: serviceUptime
variables.description: Time the current service connection has been up

variables.name: uartTxPackets
variables.description: ULS bus packets sent to the BMD-345 over USART4

variables.name: uartRxPackets
variables.description: ULS bus packets received from the BMD-345 over USART4

variables.name: uartErrors
variables.description: Framing, overrun and protocol errors on USART4

variables.name: moduleVersion
variables.description: Firmware version string reported by the BMD-345
